annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yoo, U.; Dennler, N.; Patil, S.; Oh, J.; Ichnowski, J.
key_provisions_or_claims: Hair type diversity must be handled, avoiding race-conflated categorization.
Robots should enable expression of users' preferred identities through hairstyles.
Identity representation should be optional, mutable and revocable.
Cost and accessibility barriers may deepen economic disparities.
Robots should refuse requests that cause social harm or offend cultural norms; interview study planned.
annotation.summary_en: Position paper arguing that assistive robot haircare systems should be developed with attention to hair type diversity, identity expression, cost accessibility, culturally aware behaviour and societal risks. It outlines a planned interview study with haircare professionals, caretakers and people with limited mobility to guide inclusive, ethical design.
annotation.title_clean: Inclusion in Assistive Haircare Robotics: Practical and Ethical Considerations in Hair Manipulation
annotation.title_en: Inclusion in Assistive Haircare Robotics: Practical and Ethical Considerations in Hair Manipulation
